chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Nuṣayr, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام:

And I asked him about a man who led a people in the ʿaṣr prayer, then remembered while he was praying with them that he had not prayed the first one. He said: “Then let him make it the first prayer that he missed, and restart the ʿaṣr prayer, while the people have completed their prayer.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Whoever has missed many prayers and has not counted their number, and does not know specifically which of the five they were, or all five prayers together had been missed by him for a period and he cannot count them, then let him pray four, three, and two rakʿahs at every time in which there is no constriction due to a present prayer. And let him do that abundantly until it becomes predominant in his estimation that he has made up what he missed and even exceeded it. We have explained that if what he missed is not specifically determined for him, he prays four, three, and two rakʿahs at every time. As for what indicates that he must do much of it, it is what has been established: that making up the obligatory prayers is wajib, and when their making up is established and he cannot free himself from that except by doing much of them, then abundant performance of them becomes obligatory upon him. This is made even clearer by the fact that the nawāfil, whose make-up is not obligatory, have still been encouraged to be made up; if their ruling is this ruling, then the obligatory prayers are more entitled to that. And the one who narrated that.

key_terms.الْأُولَى: the earlier prayer, referring contextually to the first prayer that should have been performed before ʿaṣr
key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: the ʿaṣr prayer, the afternoon obligatory salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: the obligatory acts, here specifically the obligatory prayers
key_terms.قَضَى: he made up or fulfilled what was due after its time
key_terms.يَغْلِبَ عَلَى ظَنِّهِ: it becomes predominant in his estimation; he reaches practical confidence

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he remembers during ʿaṣr prayer that he missed an earlier obligatory prayer, or if he has many uncounted missed prayers to make up?
ai.summary: This text addresses rulings on missed salat (prayer), especially when an Imam remembers during ʿaṣr that he had not prayed an earlier obligatory prayer, and the procedure for correcting that. It also explains the legal method for one who has many uncounted missed prayers: he should perform repeated sets sufficient to cover what was missed until he is confident he has fulfilled the obligation.
